title: Retail Installment Contracts: Charges and Credits from Other Products, and Transfers to a Deficiency Account
content:
**Ancillary charges.** On Retail Installment Contracts, an ancillary charge is capitalised only on a contract whose status is active. A force-placed insurance premium billed with the billing method "added to contract balance" is added to principal on its billing date, linked to the premium record, and accrues simple interest from then like any other principal; premiums for any other billing method never reach the contract.

**Ancillary credits.** An ancillary credit — an insurance or add-on refund, a GAP waiver benefit or an SCRA interest credit — is applied only to a contract whose status is active, repossessed or charged off. A refund that arrives after the contract is paid off or liquidated is paid by the issuing product directly to the borrower or credited to the deficiency account instead, under that product's own refund rules.

A credit reduces principal on its posting date and never advances the next due date, so the borrower's scheduled installments continue unless the credit pays the contract off. A credit larger than the payoff amount is limited to the payoff amount, and the issuing product pays the excess to the borrower.

**Balance transfer after sale.** When the repossessed vehicle is sold and a deficiency account opens, the contract's remaining principal balance and fees due move to that deficiency account on the sale date as one balance transfer, together with interest accrued to the sale date added by the deficiency account; recovery expenses are added by the recovery file, not by the contract. A balance transfer is made only from a contract whose status is liquidated.

| Posting | Contract statuses that accept it |
|---|---|
| ancillary charge (force-placed premium added to the balance) | active |
| ancillary credit (refund, GAP benefit, SCRA interest credit) | active, repossessed, charged off |
| balance transfer to a deficiency account | liquidated |

**Hypothetical cases.**

- A refund of 240.00 reaches an active contract with a payoff amount of 3100.00: principal falls by 240.00 and the next installment remains due on its date.
- A refund of 900.00 reaches an active contract whose payoff amount is 650.00: 650.00 is credited, paying the contract off, and the issuing product pays the remaining 250.00 to the borrower.
- A refund arriving after the contract is paid off is not credited to the contract.
